channel.title: Farsçadan (English)
channel.description: AI-assisted English translations of selected stories from Iran's Persian-language press. Every story notes the outlet's political orientation.

item.title: New defense minister approved by Parliament with 237 votes: "We are ready for the 4th war"
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Ahlaki approved as defense minister with 237 votes; said they are ready for a "4th war" scenario against Israel. (Source: Kayhan)

item.title: Araghchi replies to Netanyahu: 'We have unfinished business too'
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Netanyahu said Iran will recover; Foreign Minister Araghchi replied, "We have unfinished business," hinting at unresolved confrontation. (Source: ISNA)

item.title: Rubio sided with Britain on Iran's role in RAF Fairford attack plan
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington agrees with Britain's assessment of Iran's role in the Fairford airbase attack plan. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Turkey's Energy Minister: Turkey will also get a share of Russia-U.S. gasoil deal
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Turkey's Energy Minister Bayraktar said Turkey will also receive a share of the Russia-U.S. gasoil agreement; deal details remain unverified. (Source: ISNA (from Channel 7 interview, via Donya-ye Eqtesad))

item.title: Macron linked fuel price hikes to the Iran war, street violence continues in France
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Macron said France's fuel price increases come from the U.S.-Iran war; looting continues, opposition calls for his resignation. (Source: Ettelaat)

item.title: The Week in Frame (Oct. 12-18): Hormuz numbers don't add up as diplomacy continues
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: The Persian press, Oct. 12-18. Mine vs. attack accounts in Hormuz, indirect U.S. talks and sanctions, the Yemen front and the Turkey angle. (Source: Farsçadan)

item.title: Attack count disputes: TASS said 22 ships in 13 days; UK center logged 12
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: TASS said 22 ships were hit in Hormuz over 13 days; UK shipping center counted 12 in the same week; IRGC claimed two tankers hit mines. (Source: IRNA (via TASS))

item.title: Qatar: Iran's $6 billion frozen funds a trust-building card in talks
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Qatar's foreign ministry spokesman said the $6 billion in frozen Iranian funds held in Doha is a trust-building tool held during ongoing talks. (Source: Donya-ye Eghtesad)

item.title: Experts Assembly demands 'strict enforcement' of hijab; firm answer to U.S. threats
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Assembly that selects the leader issued statement demanding strict hijab enforcement and military-diplomatic readiness against U.S. threats. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Education Ministry warns against 'homeschools'; some centers sealed
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Tehran's Education Ministry says 'homeschool' centers operating outside official oversight are illegal; some have been sealed. (Source: ISNA (via Kayhan))

item.title: Government vows to expand food card support; cash aid deposited for income tiers 1-3
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Budget Organization chief said other applicants for expanded support would be reviewed; same day, October cash aid deposited to income tiers 1-3. (Source: Tasnim (via Kayhan))

item.title: Trump rejected nuclear weapons but kept 'mother of all bombs' on the table
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Trump said he won't use nuclear weapons against Iran but didn't rule out MOABs against nuclear facilities; Iran responded with a counter-threat. (Source: Hamshahri)

item.title: Supertanker hit in the Strait of Hormuz: Sepah says mine, India claims bullet strike
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: A supertanker carrying over 2 million barrels of crude was damaged in the Strait; Sepah said mine, India claimed projectile hit. (Source: IRNA)

item.title: CENTCOM claims blockade is 'impenetrable,' Reuters reports Iran selling LPG and jet fuel
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: CENTCOM commander says Iran's $25 billion oil exports are blocked; Reuters reports Iran selling LPG and jet fuel by tanker loads. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Azerbaijan's hijab ban: Ankara backs away from criticism, Kayhan calls it a 'threat'
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Turkish Foreign Minister Fidan and former PM Yildirim retracted criticism of Azerbaijan's hijab ban; Kayhan framed it as a "threat." (Source: Kayhan)

item.title: Shot in the head at a Dey protest, Peyman Kadiri dies nine months later
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Dey uprising protester Peyman Kadiri, allegedly shot in the head by security forces, died after nine months unable to exit a coma. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Turkish parties oppose Mecca Pact: 'Don't drag Ankara into Yemen war'
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Turkish political parties warned that the Mecca Pact signed with Saudi Arabia could draw Turkey into Yemen's conflict. (Source: ISNA)

item.title: Iran's top diplomat: We are seriously considering withdrawing from the NPT
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: A senior Iranian diplomat said Tehran is evaluating withdrawal from the nuclear nonproliferation treaty as a serious option. (Source: Hamshahri)

item.title: U.S. Treasury adds 16 people and 10 institutions linked to Iran to sanctions list
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: The U.S. Treasury Department targeted Iran's networks for currency and oil revenue, adding 16 individuals and numerous institutions to sanctions. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Lebanon's Central Bank revoked Bank Saderat Iran's operating license
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: According to Bloomberg, Lebanon's Central Bank revoked Bank Saderat Iran's license in line with regional restrictions. (Source: Hamshahri)
